gaps.sentence: All the tickets ___ (sell) within an hour of going on sale.
gaps.explanation: Past simple passive: were + sold. 'All the tickets' takes a plural verb.

gaps.sentence: A cheaper version of the vaccine ___ right now.
gaps.explanation: 'Right now' requires present continuous passive: is being + developed.

gaps.sentence: This wall ___ (build) centuries ago — no modern tool leaves marks like these.
gaps.explanation: Perfect modal passive: must have been + built to draw a conclusion about the past.

gaps.sentence: The novel ___ (write) in under three months.
gaps.explanation: Past simple passive (was/were + past participle): was written. The writer is not mentioned.

gaps.sentence: Passengers ___ (ask) to fasten their seatbelts before take-off.
gaps.explanation: Present simple passive: are + asked. The agent (crew) is obvious and omitted.

gaps.sentence: Over two hundred bird species ___ (record) in the valley this spring.
gaps.explanation: 'This spring' is an open time frame, so present perfect passive: have been + recorded.

gaps.sentence: These wetlands ___ (threaten) by pollution every single year.
gaps.explanation: Present simple passive with the agent introduced by 'by': are threatened by.

gaps.sentence: The bridge ___ (inspect) twice a year for signs of corrosion.
gaps.explanation: 'Twice a year' marks a routine: present simple passive, is + inspected.
